ask: Weekend sale on Instagram: here's the promo graphic with the code (https://cdn.example.com/sale-code.jpg), a 15-second clip of the shop (https://cdn.example.com/shop.mp4) and 4 product shots (https://cdn.example.com/p1.jpg to p4.jpg).

media.alt_text: Sale graphic: 15% off this weekend with code WEEKEND15

steps.why: The code graphic becomes a story: the offer ends Sunday, and a story is gone in 24 hours. A story shows no caption, which is fine because the code is in the image. One image only; a story with two fails.

arguments.content: Saturday at the shop, in 15 seconds. The sale runs all weekend.

media.alt_text: Customers browsing shelves in a bright shop

steps.why: The clip becomes a reel: video that can reach people who don't follow yet, and it stays useful after the sale.

arguments.content: Four favourites, all 15% off this weekend with WEEKEND15. Swipe for each.

media.alt_text: A ceramic mug in sage green
A linen tote bag with leather handles
A stack of three notebooks in earth tones

steps.why: The product shots become a carousel in the feed: 2 to 10 items make one whatever content_type says, each slide one product with its own alt text. No trial reel: that needs one video.
Bad Instagram values are skipped, not refused: confirm content_type STORY before saying it is a story. Same check for the reel.

say: Saved to Acme as 3 Instagram drafts. 1. A story with the code graphic, gone after 24 hours (stories show no caption, so the code in the image carries it). 2. A reel of the shop clip: "Saturday at the shop, in 15 seconds. The sale runs all weekend." 3. A 4-photo carousel: "Four favourites, all 15% off this weekend with WEEKEND15. Swipe for each." Nothing goes out yet. Same time for all three?
never: All the media on one post: it would become one carousel and the clip's reach is lost.
A story with a caption that matters: it isn't shown.
A story for one Instagram account and a reel for another on one post: two posts.
